## Load data

```{r}
#| output: false
library("tidyverse")
library("broom")
library("ggrepel")
```

Load all the library needed.

```{r}
raw_dir <- "../lab07_git_exercises/data/"
data_file <- "gravier.RData"
data_loc <- "https://github.com/ramhiser/datamicroarray/raw/master/data/"

if (!dir.exists(raw_dir)) {
  dir.create(path = raw_dir)
}

if (!file.exists(str_c(raw_dir, data_file))) {
  download.file(
    url = str_c(data_loc, data_file),
    destfile = str_c(raw_dir, data_file)
  )
}

load(file = str_c(raw_dir, data_file))
```

Importing the data using the code chunk given. Gravier is a dataset containing breast carcinoma data.

## Clean data

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug <- gravier |>
  bind_cols() |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    y = case_when(
      y == "poor" ~ 1,
      y == "good" ~ 0
    )
  ) |>
  relocate(early_metastasis = y)
```

We process the raw `gravier` dataset by transforming the variable `y` into a binary numeric variable (1 for poor outcome, 0 for good outcome) and renaming it to `early_metastasis`.

## Analysis

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long <- gravier_clean_aug |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("g"),
    names_to = "gene",
    values_to = "log2_expr_level"
  )
```

To work on the dataset, we firstly convert it into a long format dataframe (tidy structure).

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long |>
  group_by(gene) |> # Group the rows for each gene
  nest() |> # Nest each group into a separate data frame
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  group_by(gene) |>
  mutate(
    model_object = map(
      .x = data,
      .f = ~ lm(
        formula = log2_expr_level ~ early_metastasis,
        data = .x
      )
    )
  )
```

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
  mutate(
    model_object_tidy = map(
      .x = model_object,
      .f = ~ tidy(
        .x,
        conf.int = TRUE,
        conf.level = 0.95
      )
    )
  )
```

We then nest the data by gene, so that each gene has its own tibble. After that, we fit a linear regression models to evaluate the association of each gene with early metastasis. Finally, we extract the models using `tidy()`, which organizes the data into a tidy tibble.

```{r}
gravier_estimates<- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |> 
  unnest(model_object_tidy)
```

```{r}
gravier_estimates <- gravier_estimates |>
  filter(term == "early_metastasis") |>
  select(-c(2:4, 6, 7)) |>
  relocate(p.value, .before = estimate) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
gravier_estimates <- gravier_estimates |>
  mutate(
    q.value = p.adjust(p.value),
    is_significant = case_when(
      q.value >= 0.05 ~ "no",
      q.value < 0.05 ~ "yes"
    )
  )
```

Before visualize the data we create another dataset (`gravier_estimates`), by keeping only the slope term. We then add a column containing the q-value (i.e. the p-value adjusted for multiple tests).

### Visualize

```{r}
gravier_estimates |>
  filter(is_significant == "yes") |> # Take only significant rows
  mutate(gene = fct_reorder(gene, estimate)) |> # Order genes based on estimates
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = gene)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                orientation = "y") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "black") +
  labs(
    title = "Genes Associated with Early Metastasis in Small Node-Negative Breast Carcinoma",
    x = "Estimates (95% CIs)",
    y = ""
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 11)
  )
```

In the graph, genes with positive coefficients may be associated with a higher probability of early metastasis, whereas genes with negative coefficients may be associated with a lower probability.

```{r}
gravier_estimates |>
  mutate(
    label = case_when(
      is_significant == "yes" ~ gene,
      TRUE ~ "")) |>
  ggplot(aes(
      x = estimate,
      y = -log10(p.value),
      color = is_significant,
      label = label)) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5,alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_text_repel(size = 3, max.overlaps = 40) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  labs(
    title = "Genes Associated with Early Metastasis in Small Node-Negative Breast Carcinoma",
    subtitle = "Genes highlighted in turquoise were significant after multiple testing correction",
    x = "Estimates",
    y = "-log10(p)",
    color = "Significant") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.3),
        legend.position = "none")
```
